title: Optimal Output Rate for Permutation-Based DRBGs
summary: A permutation-based DRBG attains output rate 1 asymptotically, but whether any secure such generator can exceed 1 in the seedless robustness model remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a deterministic random bit generator (DRBG), define its output rate as $\rho=\frac{\text{number of bits returned by the next operation}}{\text{total output length of the underlying primitive queries consumed by that operation}}$; thus, $\rho=1$ fully uses the primitive outputs. Sponge-DRBG extracts only $r$ bits from the $n$-bit output of one primitive query, whereas the hash-function-based MD-DRBG and block-cipher-based MD-DM-DRBG attain $\rho=1$. Resolve the conjecture that $1$ is the maximum output rate compatible with security for a permutation-based DRBG in the seedless robustness model: prove that every such secure DRBG satisfies $\rho\leq 1$, or refute the conjecture by constructing one with $\rho>1$.

scope.domain: Design and efficiency of permutation-based deterministic random bit generators.
assumptions: Security is required in the seedless robustness model.
parameters: ρ: output rate of a DRBG's next operation
r: number of bits extracted by Sponge-DRBG from one primitive output
n: bit length of that primitive output
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that every secure permutation-based DRBG has output rate at most 1, or construct a secure one with output rate greater than 1.

citations.label: Enhancing Provable Security and Efficiency of Permutation-based DRBGs

progress.summary: The paper explicitly conjectures that output rate 1 is optimal and presents POSDRBG as attaining that rate asymptotically, without proving that larger rates are impossible.
citation_labels: Woohyuk Chung et al., Enhancing Provable Security and Efficiency of Permutation-based DRBGs
